name: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd
title: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd - 539254 - Transcript Of Earnings Call Pertaining To The Unaudited Financial Results Of The Company For Q1 FY 27

summary.headline: AESL Q1 FY27: Energy Solutions platform delivered about INR 570 crore EBIT on 3,325 MU long-term sales; management frames AESL as a full-scale utility.
summary.overview: Management said AESL has moved to a full-scale utility with four operating businesses (transmission, distribution, smart metering, Energy Solutions) and expects consistent quarter-on-quarter reporting. Quarterly capex was close to INR 3,500 crore. Energy Solutions is the new focus: about 5 GW of take-or-pay supply and 3,500 MWh of storage tied up, with long-term offtake being built out. Management said the IntelliSmart acquisition is pending CCI approval. Analysts pressed on the sustainability of Energy Solutions margins, which management tied to whether purchase positions are back-to-back with sales.

financial_highlights.metric: Energy Solutions EBIT (as stated on call)
financial_highlights.value: about INR 570-590 crore (speaker used both figures; INR 570 crore attributed to long-term contracted volume)

financial_highlights.metric: Power management services and trading revenue
financial_highlights.value: about INR 30 crore on about 9,800 MU (services); INR 16 crore and INR 12 crore cited for two sub-buckets

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 68 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: Management cited significant growth in Q1 and about 28,000 circuit km of lines; expects about INR 20,000-25,000 crore of annual capex additions from a roughly 25% market share, with STU and HVDC pipeline building.

segments.name: Distribution (Mumbai and Mundra)
segments.commentary: Described as growing at a stable pace; no segment figures were given on the call.

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.commentary: Cumulative 1.34 crore meters installed against a 2.46 crore order book; 21 lakh meters installed this year. Remaining balance tenders about 10-11 crore meters (100-120 million).

segments.name: Energy Solutions
segments.commentary: About 5 GW supply tied up (about 4,000 MW from Adani Green, rest third party) plus 3,500 MWh storage on take-or-pay; about 350 MW of C&I customers signed. Long-term C&I margin positions are the main EBITDA driver.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Energy Solutions revenue and results to be reported consistently quarter-on-quarter as the business reaches full scale.
Management aims to back-to-back most purchase contracts with sales contracts, keeping a few percent of capacity open for market trading.
Long-term offtake contracts on the sales side are described as being in advanced stage; no timeline given.
Expected HVDC commissioning: KPS HVDC around December 2029 and Rajasthan around beginning of 2029.
Expected annual transmission bidding opportunity of about INR 1 lakh crore; STU volume expected at least INR 20,000-25,000 crore per year.
IntelliSmart expected to have profitability similar to AESL once CCI approval and takeover complete; combined meter portfolio about 4.7 crore meters, with scope for volume growth.
Market opportunity for Energy Solutions cited as 7.5 GW-plus by 2031 (company presentation figure).
capex_capacity: Quarterly capex close to INR 3,500 crore in Q1 FY27.
Transmission: about 28,000 circuit km; expected annual capex additions INR 20,000-25,000 crore.
Smart metering: 1.34 crore meters installed cumulatively; 2.46 crore order book; 21 lakh meters installed this year.
Energy Solutions: about 5 GW supply secured, 3,500 MWh battery storage tied up on take-or-pay; about 350 MW of C&I customers.
Some last-mile transmission infrastructure capex may be needed to enable C&I contracts, but management says the model is not capex-based.
demand_pricing: Energy Solutions bilateral and exchange sales prices cited at INR 3 to INR 13-15 per unit depending on bundling and tenor; contract tenors from 1 to 13 months.
Services spread on managed-solutions business about INR 0.3 per unit in the quarter, described as service revenue rather than a true spread.
Q1 margins were lifted by delayed monsoon and high market prices; management said quarter-to-quarter variability will persist for open positions.
Data center demand from the group and third parties is growing; current data center volume is small (one contract, about 20-25 MW).
Price discovery for supply is market-linked, decided on quantum and price options at purchase.
State tender pipeline: management says STU projects are gaining momentum with Maharashtra, Rajasthan and UP active.
Parallel licence application remains pending with the regulator; management says it is waiting on a central tariff policy amendment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the smart meter balance tender pipeline and the IntelliSmart return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance tenders about 10-11 crore meters, in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and parts of Andhra and other states. IntelliSmart awaits CCI approval; profitability expected similar to AESL.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Energy Solutions book is tied up and what is the EBITDA sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants most purchase capacity tied on the sales side too, leaving only a few percent liquid, to avoid P&L volatility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread on the services and position-taking business?
qa_highlights.answer: Services earn about INR 0.3 per unit this quarter as service revenue; position-taking margins are much higher and contract-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the Energy Solutions EBIT and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 570 crore from long-term contracted volume of 3,325 MU; balance from services and trading on about 9,800 MU. About 400-500 MU is back-to-back with C&I customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 profit sustainable given the delayed monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said open positions create year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter variability; target is to close positions on both sides quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Smart meter revenue fell QoQ in presentation: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accounting treatment (capex booked as expense and revenue) explains the presentation figures; commissioned meter operating revenue rose from INR 68 crore to about INR 161-166 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Who is party to the 2.5 GW Maharashtra round-the-clock contract?
qa_highlights.answer: LOI was issued to Adani Power, but AESL expects to be a major participant and may buy power from Adani Power to fulfil the solution.

qa_highlights.question: Right-of-way challenges and STU payment mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: ROW handled at ground level in parallel with state machinery; STU payment mechanism mirrors CTU structure with distribution companies paying STU monthly.

risks_watch: Energy Solutions margins depend on open positions; management said quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year variability is expected.
Timing mismatches between purchase and sales contracts, and long-term sales contracts not yet signed for much of the volume.
Pending CCI approval for IntelliSmart and the pending parallel licence application.
Figures on call are inconsistent in places (EBIT INR 570 vs 590 crore; smart meter revenue INR 161 vs 166 crore); verify against the results release.
Data center demand timing and mix, and whether the Maharashtra RTC contract flows to AESL, remain open.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on Energy Solutions and the STU/HVDC pipeline, but cautious on margin sustainability, acknowledging open-position variability. Several answers on numbers were loose or deferred to presentation pages, and the call ran with a few interruptions.
key_quotes: In this quarter, AESL has, in fact, now transitioned into a full -scale utility.
So we would not want to have that kind of variability on our P&L.
So roughly about INR20,000 crores, INR25,000 crores of capex addition every year.
So, the gap is something which we are able to earn as revenues.

adds.what: Energy Solutions: about 5 GW supply secured (about 4,000 MW from Adani Green, rest third party) plus 3,500 MWh battery storage on take-or-pay
Smart meters: 21 lakh meters installed this year against 2.46 crore order book
STU transmission projects: expected annual capex additions INR 20,000-25,000 crore from pipeline (not yet awarded per brief)
KPS HVDC transmission line (commissioning around December 2029)
Rajasthan HVDC transmission line (commissioning around beginning of 2029)

growth.why: Management guides to consistent quarter-on-quarter Energy Solutions reporting and STU inflows of INR 20,000-25,000 crore a year, backed by about 5 GW supply, 3,500 MWh storage, a 2.46 crore smart meter order book and HVDC lines due 2029, though no explicit revenue growth percentage was given and long-term offtake has no timeline.
